---
title: "Stage 1: Shot Volume, Shot Quality, and Big Chances"
output: html_document
---

Results come from the pipeline (`targets::tar_make()` in the project root);
this report only reads and displays them. See `README.md` for the reasoning
behind each choice.

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# Run from the project root whether knit by tar_make() or by the Knit button
root <- normalizePath(if (file.exists("_targets.R")) "." else "..")
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = root)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```{r libraries}
library(targets)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
tar_source()
```

```{r read}
matches <- tar_read(matches)
shots_all <- tar_read(shots_all)
shots <- tar_read(shots)
team_match <- tar_read(team_match)
stage1 <- tar_read(stage1)
```

## 1. Data

```{r data}
cat(sprintf("Matches: %d | All shots: %d | Open-play shots: %d\n",
            nrow(matches), nrow(shots_all), nrow(shots)))
show_table(as.data.frame(table(League = matches$league), responseName = "Matches"))
```

## 2. Why only open-play shots

StatsBomb's xG is calibrated for open-play shots but underrates direct set-piece
shots, so those are excluded (penalties were excluded in the Understat work too).

```{r calibration-by-type}
show_table(xg_calibration_by_type(shots_all))
```

## 3. Team-match table

```{r team-match}
cat(sprintf("Team-match rows: %d | Zero-shot rows: %d\n",
            nrow(team_match), sum(team_match$n_shots == 0)))
show_table(as.data.frame(team_match)[, c("league", "n_shots", "npxg")] |>
             group_by(league) |>
             summarise(team_matches = n(), mean_shots = round(mean(n_shots), 2),
                       mean_xg = round(mean(npxg), 2), .groups = "drop"))
```

## 4. Summary against the Understat results

```{r summary}
show_table(build_summary_table(stage1))
```

## 5. Why volume and quality are modelled separately

If team xG followed a single Tweedie distribution, these five estimates of its
index would agree.

```{r p-compare, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
plot_p_compare(stage1)
show_table(p_compare_table(stage1))
```

## 6. Shot quality: structure and stability

```{r shape, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5}
plot_shape(shots, stage1)
show_table(shape_table(shots, stage1))
show_table(stage1$mixture$fit_table)
```

What each component is, and whether StatsBomb's xG is calibrated within it.
The top component defines a big chance.

```{r components}
show_table(component_profile(shots))
```

The mixture refit within each league and within two random halves of the
matches. Leagues should reproduce the pooled structure; halves can disagree
because smaller samples cannot always separate it, which is why the mixture is
fit once on the pooled data.

```{r stability}
show_table(tar_read(stability_league))
show_table(tar_read(stability_half))
```

## 7. Calibration of the two-part model

```{r calibration, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 6}
plot_calibration(team_match, stage1$pred_nbg, stage1$cal_nbg)
show_table(calibration_table(team_match, stage1$pred_nbg))
```
